measured_motion.reason: No retained next-command torso pose at trace 400.

selection_rule: All 400 commands, 1600 limb inputs and all observed contact losses, including brief and open losses. Original counted cycles require at least three absent post-step samples followed by recontact.
limits: Distal-body origins are not ground contact points. Release position is the original first absent post-step sample, not the last supported position. Motion decomposition uses measured torso rotation and body-relative distal position in both orders; it is not a causal intervention or ideal-joint model. An open flight has endpoint displacement, not a completed relocation. Trace 400 has no next-command native torso pose. Original evaluation, thresholds and failures are unchanged.

main_findings: Five of the six counted backward events occur entirely during scheduled stance; the other is the front-left early swing.
All three rear-left backward intervals have zero speed-clipped commands. A selected upright reference does not certify support.

The largest backward relocation includes 12.95 degrees of signed torso heading change. Measured rotation contributes -41.24 to -41.59 mm under the two coordinate-decomposition orders; these are not causal estimates.

At command 365 the front-left schedule enters phase 0 while the front-right precommand contact is already absent. The rear-left loses contact after that command. The recorded phases continue advancing during the subsequent support gaps.
The terminal front-left open flight begins at trace 395 and ends at the fixed diagnostic cutoff, not at observed recontact. The original terminal failure remains false.
interpretation.limits: The motion accounting and timing do not establish that body rotation caused contact loss or that a different schedule will restore support.

next_selected_work.question: Can a support-aware phase-progression interlock prevent beginning or continuing a scheduled swing when another scheduled-stance foot has truthful absent contact?
next_selected_work.scope: Use a distinct candidate policy; older policies remain unchanged. Define and test the bounded hold, release, timeout and phase-wrap behavior in the existing shared native scheduler. Continue to measure actual contact and apply bounded joint-only support commands while held. Retain existing evaluator, gains, caps and physical records. Use all saved V42 inputs plus synthetic boundary cases for code-path checks, not predicted physical outcomes.
next_selected_work.risks: Holding a clock need not restore a missing contact; the latched geometry can still fail to regain support. A hold can also change steering, relative phase and forward progress. No unbounded hold, invented support, hidden horizon extension or global recovery-success claim.
next_selected_work.force_aware_recovery_scope: SDK2, not this SDK1 scheduling component.
